This baseline is a controlled document. Any change to the programme dates, durations, logic, or milestone dates requires a formal Change Control Request (CCR) to be raised and approved in accordance with the Programme Governance and Approval Workflow outlined in Section 3 below.

1. PURPOSE

The purpose of this baseline is to:

- Define the approved schedule for the delivery of Project Horizon.
- Provide the basis for monitoring and controlling programme progress.
- Establish the key milestone dates against which performance will be assessed.
- Support resource planning and cash flow forecasting.
- Provide a common reference for all parties involved in the programme.

2. SCOPE

This baseline covers all activities, dependencies, and milestones within the Project Horizon programme, from the current stage through to the planned completion of the works. It includes, but is not limited to:

- Design and engineering activities
- Procurement and fabrication
- Construction and installation works
- Testing and commissioning
- Handover and close-out

The baseline does not include activities outside the defined programme boundary, such as third-party utilities diversions or client-side activities not under the control of the programme team, unless specifically identified as interface activities.

3. PROGRAMME GOVERNANCE AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW

3.1 General

The programme operates under a defined governance structure to ensure that all schedule changes are controlled, assessed, and approved before they are incorporated into the baseline.

This section describes the resource loading applied to the programme baseline. The resource loading has been developed to support the programme durations and to provide a basis for the monthly cost reports and the recruitment plan for the contractor's site team.

**7.0 QUALITY AND COMMISSIONING STRATEGY**

**7.1 Overview**

This section defines the quality and commissioning strategy for Project Horizon. The strategy
is consistent with the programme logic set out in Section 4 and the resource loading
assumptions in Section 6. The objective is to achieve a safe, compliant, and fully
commissioned facility that is ready for handover to the Trust in accordance with the
contractual milestone dates.

The strategy covers the following key areas:

- Quality management and inspection and test plans (ITPs)
- Structural completion milestones
- Commissioning of M&E systems
- Testing, verification, and handover activities

The strategy is structured around a staged approach, with each stage gated by defined
quality and completion criteria. No activity shall proceed to the next stage until the
relevant gate criteria have been met and recorded.

**7.2 Quality Management**

The quality management system for the project is based on the requirements of ISO 9001:2015
and the client's Project Quality Plan. The Contractor's quality team is responsible for
implementing and maintaining the system throughout the construction phase.

Key elements of the quality management system include:

- **Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs):** ITPs are prepared for each work package and
  identify the hold points, witness points, and review points for each activity. The ITPs
  are submitted to the client's representative for review and approval prior to the
  commencement of the relevant work package.
- **Quality Inspections:** Routine inspections are carried out by the Contractor's quality
  inspectors in accordance with the ITPs. Completed inspections are recorded on the
  appropriate inspection forms and filed in the quality records system.
- **Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs):** Any instance of non-conformance is recorded on an
  NCR. The NCR process requires the identification of the non-conformance, the root cause,
  and the corrective action required. NCRs are reviewed by the project management team and
  closed out only when the corrective action has been verified.
- **Quality Audits:** Internal and external audits are scheduled throughout the construction
  phase. The audit schedule is included in the Project Quality Plan. Audit findings are
  tracked to closure.

The quality records generated during the works are retained in accordance with the
contractual requirements and made available for review upon request.

The following key performance indicators (KPIs) are used to monitor the health and performance of the programme. The KPIs are reported monthly as part of the Monthly Progress Review (see Section 9) and are reviewed at each Programme Board meeting.

The target values and reporting frequencies are defined in Table 8.1-A below. The data sources for each KPI are identified to ensure consistency of reporting.

1. PURPOSE

The purpose of this baseline is to:

- Define the approved schedule for the delivery of Project Horizon.
- Provide the basis for monitoring and controlling programme progress.
- Establish the key milestone dates against which performance will be assessed.
- Support resource planning and cash flow forecasting.
- Provide a common reference for all parties involved in the programme.

**7.0 QUALITY AND COMMISSIONING STRATEGY**

**7.1 Overview**

This section defines the quality and commissioning strategy for Project Horizon. The strategy
is consistent with the programme logic set out in Section 4 and the resource loading
assumptions in Section 6. The objective is to achieve a safe, compliant, and fully
commissioned facility that is ready for handover to the Trust in accordance with the
contractual milestone dates.

The strategy covers the following key areas:

- Quality management and inspection and test plans (ITPs)
- Structural completion milestones
- Commissioning of M&E systems
- Testing, verification, and handover activities

The strategy is structured around a staged approach, with each stage gated by defined
quality and completion criteria. No activity shall proceed to the next stage until the
relevant gate criteria have been met and recorded.

**7.2 Quality Management**

The quality management system for the project is based on the requirements of ISO 9001:2015
and the client's Project Quality Plan. The Contractor's quality team is responsible for
implementing and maintaining the system throughout the construction phase.

Key elements of the quality management system include:

- **Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs):** ITPs are prepared for each work package and
  identify the hold points, witness points, and review points for each activity. The ITPs
  are submitted to the client's representative for review and approval prior to the
  commencement of the relevant work package.
- **Quality Inspections:** Routine inspections are carried out by the Contractor's quality
  inspectors in accordance with the ITPs. Completed inspections are recorded on the
  appropriate inspection forms and filed in the quality records system.
- **Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs):** Any instance of non-conformance is recorded on an
  NCR. The NCR process requires the identification of the non-conformance, the root cause,
  and the corrective action required. NCRs are reviewed by the project management team and
  closed out only when the corrective action has been verified.
- **Quality Audits:** Internal and external audits are scheduled throughout the construction
  phase. The audit schedule is included in the Project Quality Plan. Audit findings are
  tracked to closure.

The quality records generated during the works are retained in accordance with the
contractual requirements and made available for review upon request.

**7.3 Structural Completion Milestones**

Structural completion is defined as the point at which the primary structure of a building
or zone is complete, including the roof, external envelope, and load-bearing elements.
Structural completion is a gating milestone for the commencement of fit-out activities in
the relevant zone.

The structural completion milestones for the programme are based on the zone breakdown
defined in Section 4. The milestones are identified in the programme as follows:

**Table 7.3-A – Structural Completion Milestones**

| Milestone Reference | Description | Zone | Predecessor Activity |
|---|---|---|---|
| MS-10 | Structural completion – Zone A (Ward Block) | Zone A | Completion of roof slab and parapet works |
| MS-11 | Structural completion – Zone B (Treatment Wing) | Zone B | Completion of roof slab and parapet works |
| MS-12 | Structural completion – Zone C (Plant Room) | Zone C | Completion of roof slab and parapet works |

The structural completion milestones are defined as the completion of the following
activities:

- Completion of all structural concrete works, including slabs, columns, and shear walls
- Completion of the roof structure and waterproofing
- Completion of the external envelope, including cladding and glazing
- Completion of the structural steelwork, where applicable
- Removal of all temporary works and scaffolding from the zone

(b) the alteration of the quality or quantity of any work or materials;

The Contractor shall not carry out any variation of the Works without an instruction from the Employer's Agent, except in the case of an emergency where the Contractor takes action to protect life or property. In such an emergency, the Contractor shall notify the Employer's Agent as soon as practicable.

Any such request shall include the reason for the proposed change, its effect on the Construction Programme, and an estimate of the cost.
